chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Is Hajj obligatory on the rich and the poor?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Hajj is obligatory upon all people, their elders and their young ones. So whoever has an excuse, Allah will excuse him.'
ai.seo_question: Who is obligated to perform Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the obligation of Hajj is universal, applying to all Muslims regardless of age or wealth, provided they are capable. It establishes the principle of divine mercy by exempting those with valid excuses, such as poverty, old age, or illness, from this duty. This aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding that 'ability' (istita'ah) is a condition for obligation, ensuring the duty is not burdensome beyond one's means.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The Hajj is upon the rich and the poor?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Hajj is upon the people altogether, their elders and their young ones. So the one who has an excuse for himself, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Excuse him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from af-Fadf ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if al-Hajj is obligatory on both rich and poor people. He (the Imam) said, ‘Al-Hajj is obligatory on all people, grown up ones and small ones, only those who have good reasons Allah accepts their excuse.’”
